historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 2.8i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Land Rover Defender 110 2.8i was introduced in the late 1990s, it represented a unique, limited-production collaboration during BMW's ownership of the brand, bringing the smooth and robust BMW M52 inline-six engine to the iconic off-roader.

milestones.description: M52B28 (2.8L Petrol), 190hp, introduced exclusively for the South African market (with limited UK imports), offering a refined alternative to the traditional Rover V8 and TDi units.
End of 2.8i production, concluding this rare chapter before the wider rollout of the TD5 and subsequent Puma engines across the Defender range.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Defender 110 2.8i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 2.8i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 110 2.8i (M52B28) is widely regarded as one of the most robust engines fitted to the classic Defender, but age-related wear on cooling and valvetrain components is inevitable. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System Leaks & Overheating - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 2.8i M52B28 Suffers Thermal Stress
problems.rootCause: Plastic cooling components (expansion tanks, water pump impellers, thermostat housings) become brittle with age and heat cycles, leading to coolant loss and potential head gasket failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, and all major hoses with upgraded materials.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable preventative maintenance if caught before overheating causes head damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if overheating has warped the cylinder head or caused catastrophic failure.

problems.recommendation: For minor cooling leaks or VANOS seal degradation, targeted specialist repair is highly cost-effective and preserves the original engine. However, if the M52B28 has suffered catastrophic overheating or severe internal wear, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded cooling components is the most reliable long-term solution to protect your investment.

problems.h4: VANOS Unit Wear & Oil Leaks - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 2.8i M52B28 Loses Low-End Torque
problems.rootCause: The single-VANOS system's internal seals degrade over time, causing a loss of low-end torque, rough idle, and occasional check engine lights, compounded by age-related valve cover gasket leaks.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Installing an upgraded aftermarket VANOS seal kit and replacing the valve cover gasket.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended first step for rough idle or torque loss without full engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if VANOS failure is accompanied by severe internal mechanical damage.
